title: Cohort-Orbiter: stepwise cohorted canary policy engine
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement 'Cohort-Orbiter', a declarative canary rollout policy engine that enables cohorted step schedules, weighted traffic splits, shadow probing, and automatic rollback/attenuation guardrails. The engine should support: 1) a compact DSL for expressing staged cohorts (percent + cohort selector + duration), 2) per-step guardrails (latency P95, error-rate, semantic quality delta) with configurable evaluation windows, 3) automatic attenuation rules that drive traffic down to previous stable variant or to a mitigation variant, 4) support for shadow probes that route a configurable fraction of traffic for silent evaluation without affecting user-facing traffic, and 5) integration hooks for Console observability (per-step dashboards, alerting hooks, traces) and Release orchestration (canary TTL, pause/resume, manual override). Implementation must be compatible with both Hosted and Dedicated runtimes and expose safe SDK-level and Console-level controls. We must also provide migration paths for existing rollout configs and a developer-facing test harness for local policy simulation.
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL supports cohort selectors and weighted allocations for at least two simultaneous cohorts
Per-step guardrail thresholds can be expressed for latency, error-rate, and a custom quality metric; violations trigger configured attenuation or rollback actions
Shadow probing supports independent sampling rate and consistent KV cache isolation so probes do not contaminate production caches
Console UI surfaces step timeline, current traffic allocation, guardrail status, and a single-click rollback and pause
Automated e2e tests validate a simulated regression triggers attenuation down to 0% and notifies PagerDuty via existing alert hooks
Load-tested behavior shows stable latency under continuous batching for canaries at 5% traffic on Dedicated with autoscale enabled
Migration tool can convert at least 90% of existing canary configs in the 'rollouts' project to the new DSL format

2026-03-06 QA: Created simulation harness that replays production traces and injects latency/error regressions. Found an edge case where step timers overlap when network partition occurs; added a follow-up task.

implementation_notes: Parser implemented in rollout-service; evaluator runs in two phases (simulation + active enforcement). Enforcement leverages existing router token metadata to attach cohort tags. Shadow probe isolation implemented via ephemeral session namespaces; requires infra flag 'shadow.kv_isolation=true' on Dedicated clusters. Will add telemetry counters for 'policy_evaluations' and 'guardrail_violations' and wire to Console cost breakdowns.
testing_plan: Unit tests for DSL and guardrail logic, integration tests with router and KV cache in staging, e2e simulation using production trace replayer, canary dry-run with internal app, and chaos tests to validate timer and rollback behavior under partitioning.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives on semantic quality metric could cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: require two consecutive evaluation windows to trigger auto-rollback and provide manual override. Risk: Shadow probes could increase load; mitigation: default sampling to 0.1% and allow per-customer caps.
next_steps: 1) Land parser PR and add infra flag for KV isolation (blocked on infra team), 2) Implement Console UI components from mocks, 3) Add e2e tests and schedule a dry-run with internal product, 4) Publish playbook and tutorial for solution engineers.
notes_for_release: Feature gated behind 'cohort_orbiter' feature flag. Initial GA limited to Dedicated customers in runtime-1.19 with opt-in. Provide migration script and compatibility warnings in Console when converting older policies.
